paper_title: DLP Dynamic Layerwise Pruning in Large Language Models
caption_used: Comparison of per-output and per-layer perplexity at different sparsity rates using a logarithmic scale. Both pruning configurations maintain comparable perplexity below 10^1 for sparsity rates up to 50%, after which values begin to diverge. At 60% sparsity, the Per-Output configuration reaches approximately 15 while Per-Layer remains near 10^1. The most pronounced separation occurs at 70%, where Per-Output perplexity climbs to roughly 50 while Per-Layer reaches approximately 25. At 80% sparsity, both configurations approach 10^3, with Per-Output exhibiting marginally higher perplexity than Per-Layer at this extreme.

model_annotations.Bulgarian: The bar chart compares the perplexity of two pruning configurations, Per-Output and Per-Layer, across varying sparsity rates, with the y-axis representing perplexity on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10^0 to 10^3 and the x-axis showing sparsity rates from 10% to 80% in 10% increments. The categories on the x-axis are ordered numerically by sparsity rate, and each sparsity rate has two grouped bars representing the Per-Output (blue) and Per-Layer (orange) configurations. At sparsity rates of 10% to 50%, both configurations show similar perplexity values, with both bars at or below 10^1. At 60% sparsity, the Per-Output bar reaches approximately 15, while the Per-Layer bar remains near 10^1. At 70% sparsity, the Per-Output bar increases to approximately 50, while the Per-Layer bar reaches about 25. At 80% sparsity, both bars approach 10^3, with the Per-Output bar slightly higher than the Per-Layer bar. The legend identifies the blue bars as Per-Output and the orange bars as Per-Layer.
model_annotations.Chinese: The bar chart compares the perplexity of two pruning configurations—Per-Output and Per-Layer—across varying sparsity rates from 10% to 80%, with the vertical axis representing perplexity on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10⁰ to 10³ and the horizontal axis showing sparsity rate in 10% increments. Each sparsity rate features two adjacent bars: a blue bar for Per-Output and an orange bar for Per-Layer. At sparsity rates of 10% to 50%, both configurations exhibit low perplexity values, remaining below 10¹, with the Per-Output bars slightly taller than the Per-Layer bars. At 60% sparsity, the Per-Output perplexity reaches approximately 15 (around 10¹.18), while the Per-Layer remains near 10¹. At 70% sparsity, the Per-Output perplexity increases to about 50 (10¹.7), while Per-Layer reaches approximately 25 (10¹.4), showing a clear divergence. At 80% sparsity, both configurations approach 10³, with Per-Output reaching approximately 1200 (10².08) and Per-Layer slightly lower at around 1000 (10³), indicating that Per-Output maintains marginally higher perplexity at the highest sparsity level. The bars are arranged in ascending order of sparsity rate, and the logarithmic scale emphasizes the exponential growth in perplexity at higher sparsity rates.
model_annotations.English: The bar chart compares per-output and per-layer perplexity across various sparsity rates, using a logarithmic scale for the y-axis. The x-axis displays sparsity rates ranging from 10% to 80% in 10% increments. For each sparsity rate, two bars are shown: a blue bar representing per-output perplexity and an orange bar representing per-layer perplexity. At sparsity rates up to 50%, both configurations maintain low perplexity values, staying below 10^1. At 60% sparsity, per-output perplexity rises to approximately 15, while per-layer perplexity remains near 10^1. The divergence becomes more pronounced at 70% sparsity, where per-output perplexity reaches about 50 and per-layer perplexity is around 25. At 80% sparsity, both configurations approach 10^3, with per-output perplexity slightly higher than per-layer perplexity. The chart illustrates that while both pruning methods perform similarly at lower sparsity levels, their performance diverges significantly at higher sparsity rates.
model_annotations.German: Das Balkendiagramm vergleicht die Perplexität von zwei Pruning-Konfigurationen, Per-Output und Per-Layer, bei verschiedenen Sparsitätsraten, wobei die Perplexität auf einer logarithmischen Skala dargestellt ist. Die horizontale Achse repräsentiert die Sparsitätsrate in Schritten von 10% von 10% bis 80%, wobei die Kategorien in aufsteigender Reihenfolge angeordnet sind. Die vertikale Achse zeigt die Perplexität über einen Wertebereich von 10⁻¹ bis 10³, mit logarithmisch verteilten Beschriftungen bei 10⁻¹, 10⁰, 10¹, 10² und 10³. Zwei Balken pro Sparsitätsrate, farblich kodiert als dunkelblau für Per-Output und orange für Per-Layer, visualisieren die jeweiligen Perplexitätswerte. Für Sparsitätsraten von 10% bis 50% liegen die Balken beider Konfigurationen unterhalb von 10¹, wobei die Werte nahe bei 10⁻¹ liegen. Bei 60% Sparsität steigt der Per-Output-Balken auf etwa 15, während der Per-Layer-Balken bei etwa 10 bleibt. Bei 70% Sparsität erreicht der Per-Output-Balken einen Wert von etwa 50, während der Per-Layer-Balken bei etwa 25 liegt. Bei 80% Sparsität steigen beide Balken auf Werte nahe 10³, wobei der Per-Output-Balken leicht höher ist als der Per-Layer-Balken. Die Balken sind in der Reihenfolge der Sparsitätsraten sortiert, und es gibt keine visuellen Hervorhebungen wie Schattierungen oder Umrandungen.
